note: Hand-maintained: questions, predictions, outcomes and decisions. Every number shown alongside comes from `uv run python -m epistemics.ledger build`, recomputed from frozen artifacts.

decisions.decision: The product is an epistemic passport: a consumer reading guide, not a paper.
Naturalistic tasks are the goal; formal tasks identify parameters and dossiers test transfer.
No fresh human data collection for at least several weeks; use published human benchmarks.
The core is a formal model with interpretable parameters (computational-psychiatry style), including an HGF volatility hierarchy and a value-of-certainty term.
HGF coupling kappa stays fixed; first modules T2, T3 and T5.
Do not capture reasoning summaries: model self-reports are dominated by response bias (Meyer, Garcia & Wulff 2026). Behaviour is the evidence.
No direct API runs for now; collections use the Codex CLI on the existing ChatGPT subscription.
Every reported table is regenerated by a versioned command from frozen artifacts (the ledger).

experiments.title: Research dossiers 0.2 (harder cues)
experiments.question: Does neglect appear when structure must be inferred from matching figures and a general fact?
experiments.outcome: No neglect; one repeated arithmetic slip by Sol on a control dossier.

experiments.title: Register versus validity
experiments.question: Are fabricated-but-polished reports weighted, and informal valid reports discounted?
experiments.outcome: Third null: fabrications ignored and informal reports fully weighted in every arm.

experiments.title: Positive control on 0.3
experiments.question: Does the battery separate weaker configurations at all?
experiments.prediction: If weaker configurations show neglect, the battery discriminates.
experiments.outcome: It discriminates: Luna took fabricated figures at face value unprompted and under-bought verification; Terra and Astra (low) missed the margin fabrication.

experiments.title: Disposition model recovery (T2, T3, T5)
experiments.question: Are the dependence prior, suspicion of silence and value of certainty identifiable?
experiments.outcome: Identifiable; T2 needs structure probes; certainty functions distinguishable at material values.

experiments.title: Disposition tasks acceptance
experiments.question: Which Bayesian are Astra and Sol when base rates are unstated?
experiments.outcome: Indifference Bayesians: every missing base rate set to 50%, exact updating, zero value of certainty; identical across retest and cover.

experiments.title: Model and tasks 0.2
experiments.question: Fix pricing issues; add framing, plausibility and learning variants.
experiments.outcome: All gates passed, including learning detection and start recovery.

experiments.title: Round 2: weaker configurations, framings, learning
experiments.question: Is the 50% default caused by wording, does knowledge move it, is it learned, and do weaker configurations differ?
experiments.outcome: Default survives open framing; Laplace learning from reveals; descriptions move priors, with Sol and Astra differing on disclosure; weaker configurations differ only in precision.

experiments.title: Description-to-prior modules 0.3
experiments.question: Can a five-level description-to-prior mapping be recovered, with stated against implied priors?
experiments.outcome: Recovered at r = 0.98-0.99; wall-clock timeout added.

experiments.title: Description-to-prior acceptance
experiments.question: How do Astra and Sol map graded source descriptions to priors?
experiments.outcome: Stated equals implied; irrelevant details ignored; shared relay mapping (5-95%); Astra ignored one disclosure description set entirely.

experiments.title: Description-to-prior retest
experiments.question: Are the mappings reliable across fresh contexts?
experiments.outcome: Disclosure mappings reproduce within 0.00-0.04 (Astra's set-B disregard is stable); relay extremes stable but the baseline moved from 50% to about 30% in one set.

experiments.title: What sets the relay baseline
experiments.question: Is the relay baseline a fixed default, anchored by early descriptions, or drawn afresh per context?
experiments.prediction: Fixed default: same first answer in identical-order repeats. Anchoring: irrelevant level lower after reassuring cases than after suggestive ones by at least 0.10 in both configurations. Stochastic: variation within identical orders as large as between orders.
experiments.outcome: No anchoring. Astra: fixed 50% default. Sol: 35-40% when asked cold, 50% after graded descriptions. Mild, ambiguous descriptions varied across contexts while extremes stayed fixed (the relative-judgement reading was later not confirmed).

experiments.title: Relative judgement of descriptions
experiments.question: Are ambiguous descriptions judged relative to the comparison set?
experiments.prediction: Relative judgement: mean target contrast (reassuring minus suggestive comparison set) of at least +0.10 in both configurations. Fixed mapping: within plus or minus 0.05.
experiments.outcome: Fixed mapping: mean contrasts -0.003 (Astra) and +0.016 (Sol). Relative judgement not supported. Ambiguous descriptions vary between contexts (up to 0.2 for Sol), independently of the comparison set.

experiments.title: Between-session variance of description priors
experiments.question: How much do priors from ambiguous source descriptions vary between fresh sessions, and is the variation a shared session shift?
experiments.prediction: P1: total between-session SD of the ambiguous levels at least 0.05 in both configurations. P2: the shared session shift is the larger component in both. No directional prediction between configurations.
experiments.outcome: P1 supported: between-session SD of ambiguous description priors 0.07 (Astra, moderate) and 0.11 (Sol, unstable by point estimate). P2 not supported: variation mostly level-specific. Astra's uninformative default fixed at 50%; Sol's ranged 22-52%, with one stated-implied divergence.

experiments.title: Weaker configurations on description modules
experiments.question: Do GPT-5.6 Luna and Terra map source descriptions to priors like the GPT-6 configurations?
experiments.prediction: W1: strongly suggestive above strongly reassuring by at least 0.30 in both modules. W2: median report noise above 0.05. W3: stated and implied within 0.10 at every level in at least 4 of 6 sessions per configuration.
experiments.outcome: W1 supported in 3 of 4 cells (Luna disclosure range only 0.22); W2 supported (median noise Luna 0.51, Terra 0.32); W3 supported for Terra (5/6) but not Luna (1/6): Luna states frontier-like base rates but its forecasts do not use them.

experiments.title: Dossier transfer of description priors
experiments.question: Do description-to-prior mappings measured in the formal modules predict answers when the same cases arrive as realistic document dossiers?
experiments.prediction: X1: dossier mapping within 0.10 of the formal mapping with rank agreement at least 0.8, for Astra and Sol in both modules. X2: own formal priors predict dossier answers better than 50% priors in all four cells. X3 (own versus pooled) exploratory.
experiments.outcome: Transfer holds: own formal priors predict dossier answers within 1.4-4.0 points versus 7.7-9.2 for 50% (X2 supported in all four cells); mappings differ by 0.025-0.060. X1's rank condition failed for relays (0.6, 0.7) because the middle levels are nearly tied; met for disclosure. Pooled priors do about as well as own. Dossiers were no less stable than the formal module.

experiments.title: Unprompted dossiers and weaker configurations on dossiers
experiments.question: Without being told that relaying or selective withholding exists, do agents discount copied reports and read silence as bad news when source descriptions suggest it? Do Luna's and Terra's formal mappings carry over to dossiers?
experiments.prediction: U1: strongly suggestive minus strongly reassuring implied prior at least 0.30 in all four Astra/Sol cells. U2: irrelevant level at most 0.20 (0.50 when prompted). U3: unprompted range smaller than prompted. U4 exploratory. W1: Luna/Terra own formal priors beat 50% on dossiers in all four cells. W2: Terra coherent in at least 4/6 dossier sessions, Luna in at most 2/6.
experiments.outcome: Mappings are conditional on the mechanism being named. Unprompted, Astra and Sol treated every matching report as independent, including an aggregator with no reporters (relay priors 0.00-0.03; full neglect, U1 fails) and read silence as only slightly bad news (disclosure range 0.22-0.23; U1 fails). Irrelevant level 0.00-0.02 (U2 supported); ranges shrank in all four cells (U3 supported); full neglect predicts unprompted forecasts best (0.2-4.5 points). Luna/Terra: relay mappings transfer, disclosure do not (W1 2/4); Terra coherence fell to 2/6 (W2 fails for Terra, holds for Luna at 0/6).

experiments.title: Salience: one sentence naming the mechanism
experiments.question: Does one sentence saying the mechanism exists, without its rate, restore Astra's and Sol's description-to-prior mappings in the unprompted dossiers?
experiments.prediction: S1: strongly suggestive minus strongly reassuring at least 0.30 in all four cells. S2: irrelevant level between 0.35 and 0.65. S3: named mapping within 0.10 of the prompted-dossier mapping on average. S4 (best predictor) exploratory.
experiments.outcome: One sentence restores the discount for clear cases: aggregator 0-3% to 86-92% copied, bonus description 22-24% to 60-73% selective (S1 supported, ranges 0.52-0.92). The 50% default does not return: irrelevant level 0.17-0.33 pooled, per session near 0 or 0.50 (S2 fails); named mapping 0.12-0.22 from prompted (S3 fails). Prompted mapping predicts named forecasts best (6.6-10.7 points). Hypothesis: the 50% default is induced by being asked for the rate.

experiments.title: Default induction: asking for the base rate
experiments.question: Does asking directly for each description's base rate, in dossiers that name the mechanism without a rate, bring back the 50% default for ambiguous sources?
experiments.prediction: A1: irrelevant level between 0.35 and 0.65 in all four cells. A2: asked mapping within 0.10 of the prompted-dossier mapping on average. A3: stated within 0.10 of implied at every level in at least 5 of 6 sessions per configuration. A4 (best predictor) exploratory.
experiments.outcome: Split by configuration. Astra: asking restores the 50% default and the prompted mapping (irrelevant 0.38 and 0.48; within 0.04-0.08 of prompted; coherent 5/6) - A1-A3 hold. Sol: relay stated rates return to about 40% for ambiguous outlets but its forecasts act on 9-17% (coherent 0/3 relay, 3/3 disclosure; default 0.09 and 0.29) - A1-A3 fail. First stated-applied gap in a frontier configuration; Sol's forecasts follow its named mapping. Retest: Sol's gap is intermittent (wide in 2 of 6 sessions).

experiments.title: Sol's stated-applied gap: retest and structure probes
experiments.question: Does Sol's gap between stated and applied relay base rates replicate, and do structure probes make its forecasts use the rates it states?
experiments.prediction: R1: in 3 fresh asked sessions Sol's stated rates exceed its implied priors at the ambiguous levels by at least 0.15, at most 1 of 3 coherent. R2: with probes, Sol's forecast-only priors lie within 0.15 of its stated rates in at least 2 of 3 sessions. R3: Sol's probed mapping within 0.10 of prompted. R4: Astra's probed mapping within 0.10 of its asked mapping, coherent in at least 2 of 3. R5 exploratory.
experiments.outcome: Sol's gap did not replicate at size: fresh asked sessions +0.04 at the ambiguous levels (R1 fails); across six sessions the gap is wide in two (0.48, 0.27) and small in four - intermittent, not a trait. With probes, both configurations coherent (Astra 3/3, Sol 2/3), forecast-only priors within 0.04 of stated (R2 supported but not causal), Sol within 0.080 of prompted (R3), Astra unchanged (R4). Sol's session-to-session variation (ambiguous priors 0.09-0.17 vs 0.19-0.35) motivates a per-session discrete state.

experiments.title: Second-layer model: structure inclusion (draft)
experiments.question: Can a few abstract parameters (inclusion threshold on a salience ladder, cue-driven inclusion, session drift, default, description sensitivity) explain the unprompted, named, asked and probed results, and are they recoverable?
experiments.prediction: Draft; built after the data, so the fits are exploratory. Confirmatory test proposed: abstract urn tasks on the same ladder.
experiments.outcome: Threshold recovers well (correlation 0.98, MAE 0.16-0.21 on a 0.3-2.7 range); session drift moderately; cue weight under-covers (0.75) with a plug-in mapping. Exploratory fits: Astra theta 0.65, Sol 0.96; inclusion for an uninformative description at rungs 0-3: Astra 0.12/0.74/0.99/1.00, Sol 0.12/0.52/0.90/0.99. Shared vs family-specific thresholds indistinguishable (<=1.1 nats); shared model misfits unprompted inclusion (relays over, disclosure under). Joint fit (MCMC, stated-rate channel at the ambiguous levels): recovery theta r=0.98, w coverage 0.90, fidelity phi r=0.94; Astra theta 0.47, sigma 0.39, phi 0.97; Sol theta 0.74, sigma 0.74, phi 0.87 (mixture beats pure hypotheses; marks exactly Sol's wide-gap sessions).

experiments.title: Abstract transfer of the second layer: urn tasks
experiments.question: Do the second-layer parameters fitted to dossiers (inclusion threshold, session drift, stated-applied fidelity) transfer to contentless urn tasks, including a new hidden structure (mismatch)?
experiments.prediction: P1: urn theta within 0.5 of dossier theta per configuration. P2: inclusion for an uninformative level at most 0.35 at rung 0 and at least 0.80 at rung 2. P3: Astra phi at least 0.85. P4: structure-specific thresholds do not beat a shared threshold by more than 2 SE.
experiments.outcome: Preregistered second-layer fit did not converge (R-hat 1.4-13); P1-P4 not assessable. Two design flaws: selection records contradict the deterministic mechanism once named (agents correctly excluded), and mismatch accuracy wording is ambiguous about filing errors. Exploratory: unprompted neglect transfers fully to mismatch (all 0.00) and partly to copying (198/200 record 0.20 vs 0.95 named), not to selection (1/200 blue 0.96); mismatch-only fit converges with theta 0.69 for both (dossier 0.47/0.74); Sol's stated-applied gap recurs in copying asked (+0.15 in 2 of 3).

experiments.title: Abstract transfer, corrected urn tasks
experiments.question: With the urn design flaws corrected (per-round structures; stated accuracies clarified), do the dossier-fitted second-layer parameters transfer?
experiments.prediction: P1-P4 as in the first run, assessed only if the primary fit converges (R-hat <= 1.05); S1 per structure. C1: selection's strongest level at least 0.50 at rungs 2 and 3. C2: mismatch's strongest level at rung 3 within 0.20 of rung 1.
experiments.outcome: C1 supported: named selection keeps one mapping at every rung (1 of 200 blue 0.95-1.00 at rungs 2-3). C2 not supported: Sol's strongest mismatch level fell 0.97 -> 0.63; Astra read the clarified accuracy sentence as covering misfiling (0.00 at every named rung). Primary fit did not converge (R-hat 1.96 Astra, 1.15 Sol); P1-P4 not assessable. Per-structure fits all converged: theta selection -0.25/-0.26, copying -0.77/0.07, mismatch 2.42/0.86 (Astra/Sol); S1 holds only for Sol mismatch (0.86 vs dossier 0.74). Where both fits converged (Sol), structure-specific thresholds beat shared by 20.7 +/- 5.9 WAIC. Plain selection answers identical across all 12 sessions of both runs. Astra, not Sol, showed the copying stated-applied gap this run.

experiments.title: Second layer: thresholds per structure, partially pooled
experiments.question: How much does a configuration's inclusion threshold vary between hidden structures (dossier relay and disclosure; urn copying, selection and mismatch), and what does that predict for an untested structure?
experiments.prediction: Specified before fitting (not blind: per-structure urn thresholds known). Spread tau_theta read as generalises (90% interval below 0.5 rung), structure-specific (above) or undetermined. E1 Astra structure-specific; E2 Sol undetermined; E3 without mismatch, Astra undetermined. Recovery gates R1-R5 before reporting.
experiments.outcome: Recovery gates R1-R5 pass (theta_k r 0.97, coverage 0.93; tau coverage 0.93; 0 wrong-direction; 30/30 converged), but with five structures a 'generalises' reading was never reached (0/5 true spread <0.25). Sol (valid): tau_theta 0.84 [0.33, 1.65], undetermined (E2 holds); untested structure theta [-0.72, 1.94]. Astra: misses the validity rule (bimodal disclosure mapping, R-hat 1.69; thresholds 1.018) so E1 not assessable; exploratory tau 1.41 [0.79, 2.25], structure-specific, driven by mismatch (2.19). Without mismatch both undetermined (tau ~0.9; E3 holds). Noticing one structure does not predict another; each structure must be tested.

experiments.title: Power: structures needed to show that noticing generalises
experiments.question: How many hidden structures per configuration would the hierarchical second layer need to read 'generalises' when the true between-structure spread is small?
experiments.prediction: Surrogate (normal per-structure estimates, SD 0.15-0.45) checked against the full model at 5 structures and at 10 (spread 0.1, 8 datasets; pass if at least 4 of 8 read generalises, set before the run).
experiments.outcome: Surrogate agrees with the full model at 5 structures (readings by band; tau correlation 0.94, surrogate 0.2 lower) and at 10 (full model 5/8 generalises vs 6.2 predicted; all converged). Generalises read at spread 0.1: 3% (5 structures), 52% (8), 78% (10), 93% (15), 99% (20); at spread 0.25: 36% (10), 61% (15), 90% (30). About 115M tokens to add ten structures for two configurations. Guide reports carry-over as not shown.

experiments.title: Structure checks: prompting recommendations for named hidden structures
experiments.question: Which collection protocol gives safe prompting recommendations for one named hidden structure at the lowest cost, and what do Astra and Sol need for each catalogued structure?
experiments.prediction: Specified before running: recommendation = lowest rung whose inclusion 90% interval starts at 0.8+ (uninformative description). Gates per protocol (40 synthetic configurations each): unsafe at most 10%, within one rung at least 80%, converged at least 90%; the cheapest passing protocol is adopted.
experiments.outcome: All four protocols pass (unsafe 0-2%, within one rung 85-95%, all converged); minimal (1 session per rung, ~2.1M tokens per structure and configuration) adopted as the cheapest, at the cost of more cautious advice (two rungs too many in 15%). Checks on existing sessions, 9 of 10 valid: neither configuration reliably considers any structure unprompted; mentioning suffices for selective reporting (both) and copied readings (Astra); asking how common is needed for most others; Sol needs per-case questions for relayed sources. Astra selective silence not determined (R-hat 1.43); Astra misfiled readings not reliable, flagged as a wording issue. Guide 0.3.0 reports each check.

experiments.title: Misfiled readings reworded (tasks 0.12.0)
experiments.question: Can the mismatch named sentence say unambiguously that stated accuracy applies only to readings that do come from the urn they are filed under?
experiments.prediction: Variant urn3-named changes only the named sentence (mismatch modules); plain text and questions unchanged; task validation must pass on two seeds.
experiments.outcome: Built and validated (1,632 cases, 70 contexts, both seeds; fingerprint 704367d4). Old misfiled-readings checks withdrawn from the guide; collection pending (6 contexts, about 3.2M tokens: minimal protocol at rungs 1-3, reusing plain sessions).

experiments.title: Reworded misfiled-readings check (tasks 0.12)
experiments.question: With the accuracy clause reworded, do Astra and Sol consider misfiled readings once it is named, and what prompt do they need?
experiments.prediction: R1: strongly suggestive mismatch level at rung 1 at least 0.50 per configuration (Astra 0.00 under urn2). R2: check converges and recommends a rung. E1 both meet R1-R2; E2 Astra no longer 'not reliable'; E3 Sol's advice unchanged within one rung.
experiments.outcome: 6 contexts, 3.16M tokens, 0 errors. R1: Sol 0.96 passes, Astra 0.40 fails (was 0.00). R2: both converge (R-hat <=1.011) but both 'not reliable' (rung-3 lower bounds 0.79 Astra, 0.66 Sol). E1-E3 not supported. Rewording removed the misreading (no completion answer calls accuracy ambiguous; Astra applied misfiling fully when asked, 0.97; theta 2.42 -> 1.02) but both now switch by session between applying misfiling and judging it rare (stated 0.10-0.20 for the 50-urn sensor), and one low session per configuration keeps the minimal protocol's interval below the bar. Guide wording changed to 'does not reliably take it into account'.

experiments.title: Rate-stating rung for misfiled readings (tasks 0.13.0)
experiments.question: Can the check test whether a configuration uses a misfiling rate it is given, as the consumer action beyond prompting?
experiments.prediction: Variant urn3-rated adds one rate line per record (5, 20, 30, 40, 60%). A session follows if implied priors are within 0.10 on average and 0.20 at every level. Gates: follows when applied at least 90%, falsely follows at most 10%; task validation 0.13 on two seeds.
experiments.outcome: Task validation 0.13 passed on both seeds (1,656 cases, 71 contexts; fingerprint 73d66dbc). Rule: follows when applied 57/60 (95%); falsely follows 0/120 across four alternative priors. Collection pending: 4 contexts, about 2.1M tokens.

experiments.title: Rate-stating sessions for misfiled readings
experiments.question: When told how common misfiled readings are for each kind of sensor, do Astra and Sol forecast with the stated rates?
experiments.prediction: F1: rated rung reliable if both sessions follow (mean gap <=0.10, largest <=0.20). E1: both configurations follow in both sessions. E2: both get the advice 'state how common it is'.
experiments.outcome: 4 contexts (first collection stopped after 2 on the runner's admission reserve; 2 topped up in a second identical collection, disclosed), 2.13M input tokens. Every session forecast with exactly the stated rates (largest gap 0.001) for both configurations: F1, E1, E2 hold. Misfiled-readings advice for both is now 'state how common it is': unstated, the rate is judged and sometimes judged rare; stated, it is computed exactly.

experiments.title: Which candidate traits are general? Reanalysis of existing sessions
experiments.question: For each candidate trait, do configurations keep their relative position across tasks (generalizability study), and does a configuration's deviation on other tasks predict a held-out task?
experiments.prediction: Exploratory; no predictions. Planning input for an abstract battery built to show transfer.
experiments.outcome: Precision (log report noise) is trait-like: consistency 0.91 [0.71, 1.00], leave-one-task-out gain 0.59, sign 0.85 (6 configurations, 9 tasks); within Astra/Sol weaker (0.62, gain 0.29). Stated-applied fidelity a between-family candidate (0.75, gain 0.40; driven by Luna). Noticing threshold: Astra needs less prompting than Sol in 3 of 4 structures (selection at ceiling); consistency 0.55, gain 0.22 — earlier 'noticing does not generalise' mixed task effects with interaction. Unstated-rate default and evidence weight have no configuration variance (all ~50%, gamma ~1). Cue sensitivity does not transfer. Design: cross all configurations with all tasks, avoid ceilings, finer noise grid, preregister leave-one-task-out transfer.

experiments.title: Abstract battery v2: design for showing general traits
experiments.question: What abstract design can show whether precision, stated-applied fidelity and noticing carry over to tasks they were not measured on?
experiments.prediction: Design: 6 configurations x 6 tasks (3 formal cores x 2 surfaces), 5 sessions per cell; primary test leave-one-task-out gain > 0 with within-task permutation p < 0.05 (Holm), secondary leave-one-core-out. Power: precision 0.99 (0.92 frontier-like), fidelity 0.91, noticing 0.62-0.79.
experiments.outcome: Built: model 0.6.0 (report-noise grid to 0.01; validation passed on two seeds), tasks 0.14.0 (echo, hub, stale surfaces; task validation passed on two seeds; fingerprint 91883da3), battery_v2 analysis, recovery, presets. Precision primary (recovery 100% as estimated, 0% false); fidelity demoted to secondary after failing its recovery gate (58% < 80%).

experiments.title: Abstract battery v2: transfer of general traits
experiments.question: Does a configuration's relative precision (primary), stated-applied fidelity and noticing threshold (secondary) carry over to abstract tasks it was not measured on?
experiments.prediction: H1 precision: leave-one-task-out gain > 0 and within-task permutation p < 0.05 (6 configurations x 6 tasks). Secondary: H2 fidelity, H3 noticing, H4 leave-one-core-out; near vs far descriptive.
experiments.outcome: 150 contexts, 76.8M tokens, 0 failures (runner summary step failed after Stage 2 on a module list; fixed in tasks 0.14.1; data unaffected). H1 precision NOT supported (G -0.16, p 0.33): abstract tasks set the level for everyone; the reanalysis trait came from older formats. H2 fidelity supported as secondary (G 0.39, p 0.0002, 36/36 directions; far transfer G 0.11, p 0.0004): Luna and Terra (GPT-5.6) state rates their forecasts do not use, in every task. H3 noticing not supported (G 0.00, p 0.08). Within the four GPT-6 configurations nothing transfers (exploratory).

experiments.title: Capacity battery: design (single agent first)
experiments.question: Do capacity-limited traits (load slope of precision; vigilance threshold at matched evidential strength) transfer across abstract tasks, and do they separate configurations within a model family?
experiments.prediction: Design only. Primary: load slope (Part A) and vigilance threshold (Part B), leave-one-task-out over six tasks. Construct checks: higher effort flattens the load slope and lowers the vigilance threshold within a model.
experiments.outcome: Awaiting decisions: high-effort configurations, order and budget (pilot ~4M, Part A ~51M, Part B ~76M), context dimension, stakes.

experiments.title: Capacity battery pilot (range-finding)
experiments.question: On the high-effort GPT-6 configurations: is the top load level answered exactly, do the matched-strength audit records bracket the configurations' thresholds, and how many tokens does a session use?
experiments.prediction: Range-finding only: may change load levels and likelihood-ratio values, nothing else.
experiments.outcome: 8 contexts, 4.3M tokens, 0 errors (about 0.55M per high-effort session). Part A at ceiling: both high-effort configurations exact at every load level (tau at floor, neglect 0, repeat noise 0). Part B at floor: implied prior 0.03-0.12 across LR 1-16 (faint monotone rise). Next: widen LR to 1-65,536 (N=200); test whether the load ladder binds for low effort and GPT-5.6 before escalating it. Corrected after pilot 2: Part B was not at floor. The implied value is the structure's rate, whose ideal is 0.03-0.19 over LR 1-16; both configurations took up about half the audit evidence (uptake slopes 0.42-0.57).

experiments.title: Capacity battery pilot 2 (range-finding)
experiments.question: Does the load ladder bind for low effort and GPT-5.6, and does the widened audit range (likelihood ratios 1 to 65,536) bracket the configurations' vigilance thresholds?
experiments.prediction: Range-finding only.
experiments.outcome: 16 contexts over two collections (10 + a 6-context top-up after an interruption), 8.3M recorded tokens, 0 errors. Part A: copying ladder binds for GPT-5.6 (exact within 1.5 points at 8 readings: Terra 62%, Luna 25%; neglect weight 0.23-0.29), not for GPT-6 at low effort (88-100%); the misfiling ladder is not ordered by load (the middle level is hardest for every configuration because of one item and its repeat). Part B: no thresholds; implied rates scale with the ideal observer's at a constant fraction. Uptake slope: Astra-high and Sol-high 0.50 (selection), 0.67-0.68 (misfiling); Terra 0.60 and 0; Luna 0 and 0. LR 1-65,536 spans full neglect to near-ideal uptake.

experiments.title: Capacity battery: revised design after pilot 2 (uptake; four-level load ladders)
experiments.question: Are audit uptake and the load-curve slopes recoverable on the revised designs, and at how many sessions per cell?
experiments.prediction: Gates set before the study: correlation 0.9, 90% coverage 0.8 (agent noise band); uptake MAE 0.15 and ignore/take-up classification 0.85; neglect slope correlation 0.85.
experiments.outcome: Built model 0.8.0 (uptake fit against the ideal observer; joint load-curve fit with finer bias and noise grids), design 0.10.0 (copying 2-16 and misfiling 1-12 readings over four levels, misfiling balanced per reading, typical repeats), tasks 0.17.0. Recovery: load curve passes at 2 sessions (copying) and 1 (misfiling); uptake passes at 1 session (copying) and 3 (selection), and misfiling fails within 3 (r 0.89, classification 0.78), limited by noisy respondents and the small range of ideal rates (0.05-0.25). Pilots refitted: uptake GPT-6 high 0.46-0.75, Terra 0.53/0, Luna 0.06/0.

experiments.title: Capacity pilot 3: four-level load ladders on GPT-6 (range-finding)
experiments.question: At 16 readings (copying) and 12 (misfiling), do the GPT-6 configurations leave ceiling, and does effort order the load slope within each model?

experiments.title: Open-inference screen, stage A (spread)

Commitment index mis-oriented for F5.

experiments.title: Open-inference screen, stage B (reliability)
experiments.question: Are the stage A differences between configurations reliable on a parallel form (different data and surfaces) for F1, F2, F4 and F5?
experiments.prediction: Preregistered: per contrast, consistency ICC across forms >= 0.5 with permutation p < .05 (Holm across the 8 contrasts entering), retest r > 0.

Not consistent: F1 (0.35/0.48), F4 source (-0.13; Sol's stage A difference did not replicate). Fallback test: on fixed-answer items trust is 0.00-0.11 in all 24 cells against 0.20-0.81 on open items, so the fallback is triggered by open cases (9 triggered, 11 undetermined at the grid edge, 4 no fallback, 0 constant). Profiles fitted (report noise <= 0.5) for F4 in 7/8 configurations (open-world prior 0.05-0.30 for manuals; colleagues' lists always less complete), F2 1/8, F5 2/8. experiments.title: Coherence sets for the open-inference screen (design)
experiments.question: Is incoherence that shows only when the model is open (partitions, packing, complements, conjunction identities, nesting) a reliable and general trait, and is it a bias-variance trade-off of a Bayesian sampler?
experiments.prediction: Design only. Motivation: in F4, GPT-5.6 is subadditive (direct none 0.10-0.17, listed answers leave 0.00-0.14) while GPT-6 is coherent (gaps -0.11 to +0.06). Model: Bayesian sampler (shrinkage d, precision N), with support theory as the rival; open against computable sets; bias, variance and coherent bias separated.
experiments.outcome: Built model 0.19.0, design 0.20.0, tasks 0.29.0 (fingerprint e3e31a91): modules cohere-{num,lists,trend}-{d,e}, 20 set members and 4 anchors each, 'sets' order (members at least 4 apart). Law-based fit: atoms ~ Dirichlet(alpha) with alpha integrated out (alpha fixed at 1 read even beliefs as shrinkage: 30-45% false incoherence in F4). Validation: d recovery r 0.92-0.96, coverage 0.91-0.95, false incoherence 0-7%. Task validation passed on both seeds. Stage A (preset cohere-a, 24 sessions, about 11M) awaiting go-ahead.

experiments.title: Coherence sets, stage A
experiments.question: Do configurations violate the laws of probability on open sets (Bayesian-sampler shrinkage d > 0), more than on computable sets, and are GPT-5.6 configurations more incoherent than GPT-6?
experiments.prediction: Preregistered (design note): H1 some configurations' open-set d has its 90% interval above 0; H2 open d > computable d for most; H4 Luna and Terra above every GPT-6 configuration in each family.
experiments.outcome: 24 sessions (12 plus a 12-session top-up after the machine slept: two runs passed their wall-clock deadline and admission stopped; the partial sessions are discarded), 11.4M tokens counted, no tool errors, all anchors passed. H1: Terra (F4), Sol and Sol-low (F5); none in F2. H2 holds in F2 and F5 (8/8) and fails in F4 (2/8), mostly reflecting how informative the computable sets are. H4 fails in every family. Most answers are coherent (13 of 24 sessions within 0.02 on every open partition; disjunctions exact; nesting never violated). The incoherence is not sampler shrinkage: in F4, Terra and Sol-low give listed causes exactly 1/n and answer 'none' on top, so the excess equals the 'none' answer and falls with k (Terra 0.30, 0.24, 0.20), the reverse of (k-2)d, with a disjunction residual of 0 (partition dependence, Fox & Rottenstreich 2003). In F5, 3-bin partitions sum to 1 while 5-bin ones over-sum (Sol 1.37, Sol-low 1.24). Sol-low is the only configuration above d 0.04 in all three families.

experiments.title: Central-bank statements as sequential evidence (design)
experiments.question: When agents update the probability of a rate cut change by change through a policy statement, do their readings of the evidence and their way of combining it differ between configurations, and do they obey the laws of updating (order, path, content)?
experiments.prediction: Design only. Readings (one weight per slot) are open and expected to differ. The order and path laws may be at ceiling. Stepwise cases show only the newest change, so the path law tests integration across the trajectory.
experiments.outcome: Built model 0.20.0, design 0.21.0, tasks 0.30.0 (fingerprint 02afef8e) with the recommended defaults: modules statement-{a,b}{1,2,3} (Latin square: each sequence stepwise in orders A and B and whole across a configuration's three sessions), statement-probe-{a,b}, 'sequences' order, presets statements-a/b (24 runs) and statements-probe-a/b (Luna, Astra). 24 cases per session (sequences of 1-6 changes paired by size, 2 anchors); dilution zeta added to the model. Validation (300 simulated configurations): readings r 0.86-0.88, prior use 0.95, retention 0.93, step gain and averaging 0.80 (at the threshold, exploratory in stage A), dilution 0.57; law tests' false departures 3-6%, power 0.61-0.84 against fading, averaging, over-reaction and dilution. Task validation passed on both seeds (3,696 cases, 159 contexts). Next: datability probe (about 1M), then stage A (24 sessions, about 15M); awaiting go-ahead.

experiments.title: Statements: datability probe (form a)
experiments.question: Do configurations date the composite statements to one period, so that their answers could draw on recall of what followed?
experiments.prediction: Rewrite any statement pair that Luna or Astra places in one period above 0.6 before stage A.
experiments.outcome: Tasks 0.30 (sentences adapted from FOMC statements): every pair was placed in 2013-2019 (Astra 0.50-0.78; Luna 0.91-0.98, its four period answers summing to 1.13-1.88). Rewritten in generic central-bank language (tasks 0.31: no target range, longer-run objective, maximum employment, realized and expected conditions or sustain the expansion), and the 0.6 rule applied to answers normalised over the four periods, decided before the second probe. Tasks 0.31: none flagged (normalised maxima Astra 0.32-0.59, Luna 0.40-0.58); raw maxima still reach 0.70 (Luna, statements 31 and 34) and 0.66 (Astra, statement 34). About 2.2M tokens.

experiments.title: Statements, stage A (form a)
experiments.question: Do configurations differ in how they read changes to a policy statement, and do they obey the order, path and content laws of updating?
experiments.prediction: Preregistered (design note): H1 for at least one slot, at least three configurations depart from the median reading by 0.25 with their 90% interval excluding it; H2 at least one configuration departs from the order or path law (calibrated, Holm across configurations); H3 whether any departs from the content law. Step gain and averaging are exploratory (recovery at the threshold).
experiments.outcome: 24 of 24 sessions, 13.6M input tokens, no failures, all anchors passed. H1 fails (departures: Astra on activity, inflation and guidance; Terra on guidance; Luna on the vote; no slot has three). H2 fails: no configuration departs from the order or path law (calibrated p >= 0.58; path gaps 0.13-0.31 log-odds for GPT-6 and Terra, 0.63 for Luna, whose identical presentations differed by 1.7). H3: no answer moved on any stylistic change. Prior use at ceiling: every prior answer equals the stated market prior. Readings in the same order everywhere (guidance 1.66-2.53 per change, then inflation, then activity, risks and the vote). Evidence strongly sub-additive in every configuration and both modes: one guidance change alone moves 1.6-2.6 log-odds, the same change inside a longer statement about 0.6, and four dovish changes together about as much as one (step gain 0.43-0.62 with averaging 0.31-0.64, which trade off). Consistent with treating a statement's changes as redundant signs of one stance, which the additive model cannot separate from averaging. Exploratory: the Astra family moves 0.11-0.15 log-odds less than the others, Sol (+0.12) and Luna (+0.32, partly noise) more. Generic central-bank language is a strong situation for these agents.

experiments.title: Exploration: statements post hoc and a sweep across every collection
experiments.question: Which regularities in the behaviour already collected suggest experiments where configurations differ?
experiments.prediction: Exploratory; no test.
experiments.outcome: Statements: the announced number of changes sets the weight of each change (first step 1.93 log-odds when one change is announced, 0.51 among six; step = const + b/n, R2 0.78-0.87), which neither an independent- nor a correlated-evidence Bayesian predicts; configurations nearly interchangeable (36-52% identical answers, Luna apart). Sweep (44 collections, 755 sessions, 17,728 answers): output per case tracks effort (rho 0.81); GPT-5.6 departs from the consensus and answers more boldly (rho 0.39, 0.30); within GPT-6, Astra answers open cases in round numbers and Sol in fine-grained ones at every effort (13 of 13 comparisons), with about half Sol's output per case. Ideas: vary the announced count; redundant against independent sources; deliberation style (judge against compute) and its link to incoherence; roundness as an uncertainty report; GPT-5.6 boldness as a general trait. Roundness check (screen F2, F4, F5; 72 sessions): roundness does not rise with openness within open cases for any configuration, and its relation to determinate cases depends on the configuration; extremity confounds it (checked on mid-range answers). In the Sol family, round answers sit 0.3-1.1 log-odds nearer the fitted fallback than fine-grained ones (a round answer flags a default), the reverse in Terra and Luna; the fitted trust varies too little to calibrate against. Supports the deliberation-style reading more than roundness as a general uncertainty report.

experiments.title: Deliberation style: judging against computing (design)
experiments.question: Do the GPT-6 variants differ in how they answer open questions, Astra by judgement (coarse readout, anchorable) and Sol by computation (fine readout, fuller adjustment)?
experiments.prediction: Design only. Two modules on the screen's trend cases: ladders (six nearby thresholds per series) for readout grain rho and plateaus; comparative anchors (low and high, 30 points either side of the observer's middle answer) for the anchoring weight a against the agent's own unanchored answer. Predictions: Astra's rho above Sol's at each effort; more plateaus; a differs (Astra higher); a falls with effort; Sol slower per case.
experiments.outcome: Built model 0.21.0, design 0.22.0, tasks 0.32.0 (fingerprint 59238317) with the recommended defaults: modules deliberation-ladder (four trend series x six thresholds, five points apart for a broad observer, each series' questions four cases apart) and deliberation-anchor-a/b (comparison then estimate, anchors 30 points either side, forms swapping sides); generic choice options; preset deliberation-pilot (24 runs). rho from the share of mid-range answers at multiples of 5 beyond chance; a from the high and low anchors' estimates (own answer cancels). Validation (300 simulated configurations): rho r 0.92, coverage 0.90; a r 0.96, coverage 0.87; confusion at most 0.17. Task validation passed on both seeds (3,768 cases, 162 contexts). Pilot (about 13M) awaiting go-ahead.

experiments.title: Deliberation style pilot (grain and anchoring)
experiments.question: Do Astra and Sol differ in readout grain and in adjustment from anchors, as judging and computing styles predict?
experiments.prediction: Written down before collection: P1 Astra's rho above Sol's at each effort; P2 more plateaus; P3 anchoring weight differs (Astra higher); P4 anchoring falls with effort; P5 Sol slower per case.
experiments.outcome: 24 of 24 sessions, 11.8M input tokens, no failures; ladders monotone (one violation), comparisons consistent (100%, Terra 96%). P1 holds pooled (3 of 3, intervals separate) but only through the anchor sessions: Astra rounds 67-92% of its estimates after a comparison and 8-17% of its ladder answers; Sol is fine-grained in both. P2 fails (no plateaus but Luna's). P3 fails: nobody is anchored (a -0.03 to 0.05). P5 fails (Astra not faster; Sol writes twice the output). New: a frame shift. After a comparison, Sol, Luna and Terra give more moderate probabilities than on the ladder at the same thresholds (|log-odds| -0.26 to -1.07), whatever the anchor; Astra and Astra-low do not move. Declared-uninformative anchors are at ceiling.

experiments.title: Deliberation follow-up: the anchored thresholds asked directly
experiments.question: Is it the comparison, or the number of thresholds per series and the order, that switches Astra to round answers and moderates Sol's, Luna's and Terra's?
experiments.prediction: Exploratory: if the comparison is the cause, bare answers resemble the ladder's in grain and extremity.
experiments.outcome: 8 of 8 sessions, 3.8M input tokens, no failures; tasks 0.33.0. The comparison switches Astra to round answers (67-92% after a comparison, 17-33% asked directly, 8-17% on ladders); Sol is fine-grained in every frame. The extremity shift is not one effect: the comparison moderates Sol and Terra; for Luna and Sol-high the six-threshold ladder is the extreme frame; for the Astra family a lone direct question gives the most extreme answers. Twelve single answers per configuration and frame: noisy.

experiments.title: Deliberation: which first question switches Astra's readout
experiments.question: Is it the comparison, the restated anchor, judgement framing or any preceding question that switches Astra to round answers?
experiments.prediction: Exploratory: four first questions (comparison with and without the anchor restated, likely or unlikely, the growth model) before the estimate.
experiments.outcome: 12 of 12 sessions (six GPT-6 configurations x two forms), 6.1M input tokens, no failures; tasks 0.34.0. Any preceding question switches Astra to round answers (pooled 67-72% after each kind, against 28% asked directly and 11% on ladders); Astra-high is the least affected (33-50%); Sol stays fine-grained (11-28%). The trigger is being asked as a follow-up, not the first question's content; a follow-up within a pair cannot yet be told from a session made of pairs. Quality (exploratory, against each configuration's own ladder): Astra's round follow-ups are not worse; they are nearer its own curve (0.22-0.32 log-odds) than its fresh direct answers (0.35-0.60), discriminate between thresholds like the ladder, never violate monotonicity and repeat best (0.26-0.38). Sol's follow-ups move further from its curve (Sol-low 1.19 against 0.52 direct) and repeat less well (0.49-0.62): Astra changes how it reports, Sol what it reports.

experiments.title: Follow-up rounding on the peer-advice cases
experiments.question: Does a preceding likely-or-unlikely question round Astra's probabilities on another family, open and computable?
experiments.prediction: Exploratory: sixteen peer-advice cases, eight fresh and eight follow-ups mixed per session, forms swapping them; open and stated variants.
experiments.outcome: 24 of 24 sessions (six GPT-6 configurations x four modules), 12.9M input tokens, no failures; tasks 0.35.0. Stated (computable): every configuration exact, fresh or follow-up (error 0.01). Open: Astra's follow-ups rounder than its fresh answers (pooled 25% to 42%), much less than on the trend cases (28% to 72%); Sol's not (35% to 23%); Astra's follow-ups mostly repeat its fresh answer (matched gap 0.08-0.12, Astra-high 0.58). Family and the mixed session are confounded.

experiments.title: Framing sensitivity in the passport (readout against content)
experiments.question: How should the split between changing how precisely a configuration reports and changing what it reports read in the passport?
experiments.prediction: Record: a reading-guide topic computed from the deliberation and follow-up collections.
experiments.outcome: Reading guide 0.5.0 adds 'How a question's framing changes its numbers'; the passport carries frame_sensitivity per configuration; the dashboard's passport table shows round answers fresh against follow-up. Rules: readout changes when round answers differ by at least 25 points, content when follow-ups sit at least 0.25 log-odds further from the configuration's own ladder than its fresh answers. Readings: the three Astra configurations rounder as follow-ups with the same answers; Sol-low the same precision with answers that move; Sol, Sol-high and Terra unchanged; Luna finer as a follow-up. Each reading marked exploratory; computed answers exact either way. The passport note lists framing sensitivity as a dimension.

experiments.title: Statements: announced count, with content controlled
experiments.question: Does the number of changes a statement is declared to hold set the weight of one reported change, and is that a budget by count or a pragmatic reading?
experiments.prediction: Exploratory test of exploration idea 1: one change reported in statements declared to differ in 1, 3 or 6 places, the rewordings disclosed in one condition; a budget predicts three-said = three, the pragmatic reading three-said = one.
experiments.outcome: 16 of 16 sessions (Astra, Sol, Luna, Terra x four forms), 8.8M input tokens, no failures; tasks 0.36.0. With content controlled, a single change moves 0.59-0.87 log-odds and the same change among three or six about 20% less (ratios 0.76-0.87; Terra 1.00): stage A's 1.93 came mostly from its one-change statement's content (guidance to a further rise). For Astra and Sol, disclosing the rewordings restores the full step (1.00, 0.85): pragmatic, not a budget. Guidance moves most (0.91 alone).

experiments.title: Statements: are changes treated as correlated?
experiments.question: When a statement's second change is revealed, does it move the answer as much as when it comes first (independent evidence), less when it agrees and more when it disagrees (correlated changes), or towards the average?
experiments.prediction: Exploratory test of exploration idea 21: step2(X) = a step1(X) + b step1(other); independent a = 1, b = 0; correlated b < 0; averaging a = 1/2, b = -1/2.
experiments.outcome: 16 sessions (Astra, Sol, Luna, Terra x four forms; one failed at its start on a provider capacity error with no answers, so seven runs were topped up unchanged), about 12M input tokens. Astra adds the two changes as independent evidence (a 1.04, b 0.01); Sol nearly (0.85, -0.05); Luna a hint of correlation (b -0.16, interval including 0); Terra discounts the second change by a third either way (a 0.65, b 0.02), so its final answers depend on order (gap 0.49 against Astra's 0.14). No averaging. With the announced-count result this supersedes stage A's 'strong sub-additivity', which compared one strong change with different changes.

experiments.title: Exploration: primacy across the sequence data
experiments.question: Does Terra's discount on later changes recur across the sequence data where order was varied, and does any other configuration show one?
experiments.prediction: Exploratory; no test. The same change later against first, in statements stage A (first and last positions) and the correlated changes (second and first).
experiments.outcome: Terra's primacy replicates across the two designs: a change counts about 20% less when it comes later (0.79 [0.64, 0.97] in stage A, 0.78 [0.68, 0.88] in the correlated changes). No other configuration shows a consistent position effect (Astra 0.91 and 1.03; Sol 0.97 and 0.98; Luna 1.11 and 0.99). Both datasets are statements: generality beyond the family is untested.

experiments.title: Primacy beyond statements: analysts' calls in order
experiments.question: Does Terra discount a later piece of evidence outside the statements, and are two analysts' calls added as independent evidence?
experiments.prediction: Exploratory test of idea 24: two analysts' calls without a record, one then both, each item in both orders; the correlated-changes and primacy analyses.
experiments.outcome: 16 of 16 sessions (Astra, Sol, Luna, Terra x four forms), 7.7M input tokens, no failures; tasks 0.38.0. Terra's primacy does not clearly carry over: a later call counts 0.95 [0.86, 1.06] of a first (statements 0.79 and 0.78); regression a 0.85. Every configuration treats the two calls as independent evidence (b about 0); Sol adds them exactly (a 1.01, order gap 0.11); Luna inconsistent and noisy; Terra's single-call steps are about twice the others' (1.3-1.4 against about 0.7).

experiments.title: Exploration: how strongly configurations react to an analyst's call
experiments.question: Is Terra's strong reaction to a single analyst's call general across the peer-advice data, and what drives it?
experiments.prediction: Exploratory; no test. Call weight (answer minus stated prior, signed by the call) on cases without the agent's own reading, across the multi-agent pilot and open collections, the confidence-transfer collections and the calls experiment.
experiments.outcome: With records stated every configuration gives a call exactly its record's weight (ratio 1.00). Without a record Terra takes an analyst's confident wording at face value: a 'definitely... confirmed' call moves it 2.45 and 2.60 log-odds in two independent collections, about twice the others (0.69-1.41); plain calls more too. Not for the same confidence from an AI agent (ordinary) or a sensor (no weight). Luna gives relayed calls no weight. A passport candidate: give track records, or discount confident wording.

experiments.title: Analysts' calls in the passport (face value, wording, stated records)
experiments.question: How should a configuration's reaction to an analyst's confident call without a record read in the passport?
experiments.prediction: Record: a reading-guide reading computed in the ledger build from the multi-agent pilot and open, confidence-transfer and calls-order collections.
experiments.outcome: Reading guide 0.6.0 adds 'confident-calls' under how it weighs evidence; the passport carries call_reaction per configuration; the dashboard's passport table shows the confident-call weight against the others' median. Rules: face value at 1.5 times the median of the other configurations; wording barely matters when a confident call moves it less than 0.3 log-odds further than an 'I think' call; record weighed exactly when the stated-record ratio is within 0.05 of 1. Readings: Terra face value (2.53 log-odds, to 93%, 2.4 times the others' median 1.07); Sol and Luna like the others (1.2 and 0.8 times); Astra wording barely matters (0.82 against 0.63 for 'I think', analysts only); all four exact with records. Exploratory; analysts' calls on urn cases only.

experiments.title: Confident wording across families (urn, policy note, inspection report)
experiments.question: Is Terra's face-value reaction to an analyst's confident call a trait of confident wording across families, or specific to the urn family and its phrase?
experiments.prediction: Exploratory test of idea 28: one claim without a record in four wordings ('I think', plain, 'definitely', 'definitely... confirmed') in three families, a Latin square per family. A trait: Terra's top-phrase weight at least 1.5 times the others' median, interval above 1, in every family.
experiments.outcome: 48 of 48 sessions (Astra, Sol, Luna, Terra x three families x four forms), 22.9M input tokens, no failures; tasks 0.39.0. Terra's urn face value did not replicate under a four-wording set (top phrase 2.19 log-odds, 1.29 [0.97, 1.68] times the others' median; the others gave the phrase much more than in the three-wording collections). Policy notes: Luna 2.20 and Terra 1.75 times the others' median, half of Terra's answers at 99% or more; Astra and Sol barely move with wording. Inspection reports move everyone near the ceiling; Luna and Terra furthest. 'Confirmed' adds to 'definitely' for everyone. Across families Astra is the least wording-sensitive and Terra in the top two. The passport's calls readings (Terra face value, Astra wording barely matters) overstate design-conditional effects; candidate replacement: an ordinal cross-family wording-sensitivity reading.
